paper.title: Asymptotically Optimal Fixed-Budget Best Arm Identification with Variance-Dependent Bounds

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-budget BAI with contextual information, local location-shift bandit models
unmapped: Local location-shift bandit models: absolute continuity, invariant context distribution, Lipschitz relation between conditional variance and mean, unique conditional variance under null models bounded below, bounded moments of all orders, parallel shift condition
Goal is the arm with highest unconditional (context-marginalized) mean; contexts observed before drawing an arm
Worst-case (minimax) evaluation of expected simple regret over the model class
settings.definition_quote: a decision maker observes contextual information (covariate) $X_t\in\mathcal{X}$ and draws a treatment arm $A_t \in [K]$ ... Our goal is to find a treatment arm with the highest expected outcome marginalized over the contextual distribution of $X_t$ with a minimal expected simple regret after observing the outcome in the round $T$.

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-budget BAI without contextual information, local location-shift bandit models
unmapped: Local location-shift bandit models: unique variance under null models bounded below, Lipschitz variance-mean relation, bounded moments
Worst-case (minimax) evaluation of expected simple regret over the model class
settings.definition_quote: Our result generalizes BAI without contextual information, where $\mathcal{X}$ is a singleton. Let $(\sigma^a)^2$ be the unconditional variance of $Y^a_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed fixed-budget BAI with contextual information, local location-shift bandit models
unmapped: Goal is the arm with highest context-marginalized mean
Worst-case (minimax) evaluation of expected simple regret
settings.definition_quote: For two-armed bandits ($K=2$), we can refine the lower bound as follows. In this case, we can also obtain an analytical solution of the target allocation ratio even when there is contextual information.

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed Gaussian bandits with fixed variances (P^G), no context
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{P}^G \subset \mathcal{P}^*$ denote two-armed Gaussian bandits defined in \citet{Kaufman2016complexity} with fixed variance $(\sigma^1)^2. (\sigma^2)^2 > 0$.

algorithms.name: AS-AIPW (Adaptive Sampling - Augmented Inverse Probability Weighting) strategy

symbols.Omega_ctx: inf over allocation rules w of max_a E^X[(sigma^a(X))^2 / w(a|X)], sigma^a(x) the conditional std of arm a under null models

conditions: under any null consistent strategy
local location-shift bandit models (Definition 3.2)

source.label: thm:null_lower_bound
source.quote: Under any null consistent strategy, as $T\to \infty$, \sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}^*} \sqrt{T}\mathbb{E}_P[r_T(\pi)(P)] \geq \frac{1}{12}\inf_{w\in\mathcal{W}}\max_{a\in[K]}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}^X\left[{\left(\sigma^{d}(X)\right)^2}/{w(a|X)}\right]} + o(1).

results.notes: Worst-case expected simple regret over the class; stated as sqrt(T)*sup regret >= c + o(1), recorded as liminf with c/sqrt(T). Restricted to null consistent strategies.

conditions: under any null consistent strategy
local location-shift bandit models; sigma_i is the variance-defining std of arm i under null models

source.label: cor:null_lower_bound
source.quote: Under any null consistent strategy, \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}^*} \sqrt{T}\mathbb{E}_P[r_T(\pi)(P)] \geq \frac{1}{12}\sqrt{\sum_{a\in[K]}\left(\sigma^a\right)^2} + o(1)\] as $T\to\infty$, where the target allocation ratio is $w^*(a) = \frac{\left(\sigma^a\right)^2}{\sum_{b\in[K]} \left(\sigma^b\right)^2}$.

results.notes: No-context case; target allocation proportional to variances.

symbols.Sigma_12: E^X[(sigma^1(X) + sigma^2(X))^2], conditional standard deviations under null models

conditions: under any null consistent strategy
local location-shift bandit models

source.label: thm:twoarmed_null_lower_bound
source.quote: When $K = 2$, under any null consistent strategy, \sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}^*} \sqrt{T}\mathbb{E}_P[r_T(\pi)(P)]\geq \frac{1}{12}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}^X\left[\left(\sigma^{1}(X) + \sigma^{2}(X)\right)^2\right]} + o\left(1\right) as $T \to \infty$, where the target allocation ratio is $w^*(a|x) = \sigma^a(x) / (\sigma^1(x) + \sigma^2(x))$

results.notes: Neyman-type allocation ratio of standard deviations.

bound.regime: for any eps_alg > 0 and all T > T_0(eps_alg, P)

symbols.V_i: asymptotic variance V^{a*,a}(P) of the HIR estimate of the gap between the best arm and arm i

conditions: fixed P in the local location-shift class
bound is on P(mu_hat^{a*} <= mu_hat^{a}) for a fixed suboptimal arm a

bound.regime: for any eps_alg > 0 and all T > T_0

symbols.V_i: asymptotic variance V^{a*,a}(P) of the HIR gap estimator for arm i

conditions: fixed P in the local location-shift class

source.label: thm:upper_exp_sr
source.quote: For the TS-HIR strategy $\pi^{\mathrm{HIR}}$ and any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $T_0 > 0$ such that for all $T > T_0$, \mathbb{E}_P\left[r_T\left(\pi^{\mathrm{HIR}}\right)(P)\right] \leq \sum_{a\in[K]}\Delta^{a}(P)\exp(...)

symbols.V_max: max over a != b of E^X[(sigma^a(X))^2/w*(a|X) + (sigma^b(X))^2/w*(b|X)]

conditions: no contextual information or the context space is discrete
local location-shift bandit models

source.label: thm:minimax_opt_HIR
source.quote: For the TS-HIR strategy $\pi^{\mathrm{HIR}}$, when $K\geq 3$, as $T\to\infty$, \sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}^*}\sqrt{T}\mathbb{E}_P\left[r_T\left(\pi^{\mathrm{HIR}}\right)(P)\right]\leq \max_{a,b\in[K]:a\neq b}\sqrt{\log K\mathbb{E}^X[...]} + o(1)

results.notes: Worst-case regret; stated as sqrt(T)*sup <= c + o(1), so recorded as limsup c/sqrt(T).

conditions: two-armed Gaussian bandits with fixed variances
results.notes: Lower bound on the error exponent of the misidentification probability (equivalently, an upper bound on the error probability); quantity 'other' because it bounds the exponent.

symbols.V_i: asymptotic variance V^{a*}(P) of the AIPW gap estimator between the best arm and arm i

conditions: Assumption I.1: nuisance estimators converge in probability
local location-shift bandit models

source.label: lem:large_dev
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{asm:almost_sure_convergence}, for any $P_{0}\in\mathcal{P}^*$ and all $a, b$, -\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\log \mathbb{P}_{0}\left(\widehat{\mu}^{\mathrm{AIPW}, a^*(P)}_{T} \leq \widehat{\mu}^{\mathrm{AIPW}, a}_{T}\right) \geq \frac{(\Delta^a(P))^2}{2V^{a*}(P)} - O\left((\Delta^a(P))^3\right).

results.notes: Error-exponent bound for the AS-AIPW strategy; the statement's sign placement (-liminf) appears garbled; interpreted as a lower bound on the exponent minus O(Delta^3).

conditions: no contextual information or the context space is discrete

source.label: thm:minimax_opt_HIR
source.quote: Because we can obtain an analytical solution of $w^*$ when $K = 2$ ... we have the following upper bound in those case: \sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}^*}\sqrt{T}\mathbb{E}_P\left[r_T\left(\pi^{\mathrm{HIR}}\right)(P)\right]\leq \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}^X\left[\sigma^1(X) + \sigma^2(X)\Big)^2\right]} + o(1) when $K = 2$

results.notes: Stated in the text right after Theorem 5.4 (which formally covers K>=3) as a consequence; not a separately numbered statement. Constant differs from the 1/12 in the lower bound despite the paper's claim that they match.

conditions: no contextual information

source.label: thm:minimax_opt_HIR
source.quote: \sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}^*}\sqrt{T}\mathbb{E}_P\left[r_T\left(\pi^{\mathrm{HIR}}\right)(P)\right]\leq 2\log K\left(\sqrt{\sum_{a\in[K]}\mathbb{E}^X\left[\left(\sigma^{a}(X)\right)^2\right]}\right) + o(1) when $K \geq 3$, and there is no contextual information.

results.notes: Specialisation of Theorem 5.4 stated in text; the log K factor is as printed (inconsistent with sqrt(log K) in the theorem).
